name: EFF-Interaction-v1-diagnostic
claim: Differentiable hydrophobic-contact, idealized missing-valence-cone heavy-atom hydrogen-bond, screened formal-charge-group, aromatic, halogen-bond, and profile-dispatched metal-coordination guidance. All seven implemented terms are enabled in the user-requested diagnostic default. Metal attraction is admitted only for a standalone mononuclear site with a profile-supported identity, complete retained coordination shell, one resolved vacancy, and matching geometry; otherwise attraction fails closed while an explicitly profiled repulsion-only site remains traceable. This is a pose-guidance diagnostic, not explicit-hydrogen geometry, partial-charge electrostatics, solvation, affinity, free energy, or an external docking-score implementation.

functional_form.hydrogen_bond_contact: q_DA = exp(-0.5*((r_DA-r0)/sigma_r)^2) * quintic_switch(r_DA; switch_distance, cutoff) * cone_gate(cos_D; target_D, donor_half_width) * cone_gate(cos_A; target_A, acceptor_half_width) * axis_quality_D * axis_quality_A
functional_form.screened_formal_charge: R_a = sum_i(W_ai*x_i); rho_ab = sqrt(||R_a-R_b||^2 + alpha^2); E_ab = (k_e/epsilon_r)*Q_a*Q_b*exp(-kappa*rho_ab)*Q5((r_off^2-||R_a-R_b||^2)/(r_off^2-r_on^2))/rho_ab
functional_form.aromatic_ring_geometry: For ring center C and stored non-collinear ring triplet vectors a,b, n=normalize(cross(a,b)); q_collapse=Q5((||cross(a,b)||^2-(0.25*A_ref)^2)/((0.75*A_ref)^2-(0.25*A_ref)^2)). A fused aromatic system is one saturating site, while each constituent ring retains its own center and normal.
functional_form.pi_stacking: For ligand/protein ring displacement Delta, d2=||Delta||^2, c2=(dot(n_l,n_p))^2, o_l2=d2-(dot(Delta,n_l))^2, o_p2=d2-(dot(Delta,n_p))^2. A_parallel=Q5((c2-0.75)/0.25), A_T=Q5((0.25-c2)/0.25), O=1-(1-S2(o_l2;1.5,2.0))*(1-S2(o_p2;1.5,2.0)), R=S2(d2;4.5,5.5), w=R*O*(A_parallel+A_T)*q_l*q_p; fused-system soft-OR and symmetric site saturation precede E=-epsilon*occupancy.
functional_form.cation_pi: For a declared +1 formal-charge-group center and a neutral carbocyclic aromatic ring, d2 and face offset o2=d2-(dot(Delta,n_ring))^2; w=S2(d2;4.5,6.0)*S2(o2;1.5,2.0)*q_ring. Both ligand-cation/protein-ring and protein-cation/ligand-ring directions are evaluated; fused-system soft-OR and symmetric site saturation precede E=-epsilon*occupancy.
functional_form.halogen_bond: For ligand C-X and protein acceptor A, u_sigma=normalize(x_X-x_C), v=normalize(x_A-x_X), c_sigma=dot(u_sigma,v), s=||x_A-x_X||/(R_vdw(X)+R_vdw(A)); w=S(s;1.00,1.15)*cone_gate(c_sigma;1,40 deg)*acceptor_cone_gate*CX_bond_quality*acceptor_axis_quality. Donor-X soft-OR precedes E=-epsilon*occupancy.
functional_form.metal_coordination: For each admitted metal profile m with one resolved vacant coordination slot, v_m=-normalize(sum_j normalize(R_mj-M_m)); A_mi=exp(-(1-dot(normalize(x_i-M_m),v_m))/tau_theta); Delta_r_mi=||x_i-M_m||-r0_m(element_i); eligible profile-supported donor pairs use E_pair=S(r)*D*(exp(-2*a*Delta_r)-2*A*exp(-a*Delta_r)); q_mi=S_CN(r)*exp(-0.5*((r-r0_m)/sigma_r)^2)*A_mi; CN_m=N_fixed,m+sum_i(q_mi); E_over=k_over*relu(CN_m-CN_target,m)^2; E_slot=k_slot*sum_{i<j}(q_mi*q_mj). Site-specific ineligible ligand atoms receive only bounded short-range repulsion. Profiles with attraction disabled receive repulsion and trace metadata but no Morse attraction.
functional_form.polar_unsatisfied_proxy: Trace only and dimensionless: B_i=softOR_j S(distance_to_protein_heavy;3.0,4.5); H_i=softOR(valid_hydrogen_bond_weights,admitted_metal_occupancy); u_i=B_i*(1-H_i). It contributes no energy, force, ranking score, or sampler correction.
functional_form.site_saturation: q_ij is clamped to [0,1] before q_i = 1 - product_j(1 - (1-delta)*q_ij); E = -epsilon*sum_i(q_i), with ligand hydrophobes or hydrogen-bond donors as the saturated sites
functional_form.direction_proxy: axis = normalize(sum_heavy_neighbor(normalize(atom_coordinate - neighbor_coordinate))); the target cosine around this axis is derived from an idealized linear, trigonal, or tetrahedral missing-valence cone
functional_form.cone_targets: linear degree 1: 1; trigonal degree 1/2: 0.5/1; tetrahedral degree 1/2/3: 1/3, 1/sqrt(3), 1
functional_form.cone_gate: C2 quintic rise/fall around target cosine with an angular half-width; compactly zero outside the target cone window
functional_form.axis_quality: Each normalized heavy-bond direction is multiplied by a C2 bond-length quality. rho = norm(sum weighted bond directions); site_quality = product(bond_quality) * Q5((rho-zero_below)/(full_above-zero_below)); the H-bond pair weight is multiplied by donor and acceptor site quality

aromatic_ring_typing.ligand: Neutral sanitized five- and six-member aromatic rings, including neutral N/O/S heteroaromatics, are admitted for pi stacking. Charged rings are excluded. Rings are grouped into connected fused systems; centers and normals are evaluated per elementary ring and soft-OR saturated once per fused system. Cation-pi uses the narrower neutral-carbocyclic subset.
aromatic_ring_typing.pi_stacking_histidine_policy: Neutral HIS, HID, and HIE rings are admitted for pi stacking; explicitly charged HIP is excluded. This geometry-only aromatic admission does not alter hydrogen-bond or charge typing.
aromatic_ring_typing.cation_pi_acceptor_policy: Only neutral carbocyclic aromatic systems are admitted. Protein acceptors are PHE, TYR, and TRP. HIS is excluded because its protonation and pi electrostatics are ambiguous in the current receptor boundary.
aromatic_ring_typing.ring_triplet_policy: Each ring stores one deterministic, non-collinear atom triplet and its input reference cross-product norm A_ref. Coordinate collapse is smoothly suppressed at 0.25 to 0.75 times A_ref.
aromatic_ring_typing.aromatic_overlap_policy: Hydrophobic contact remains the generic carbon-contact baseline and pi stacking is a small orientation-specific correction. Their geometric overlap is traced explicitly, but neither term suppresses the other: atom-site hydrophobic and ring-system pi normalizations are incompatible, and direct suppression can make adding a favorable pi term increase the total energy. Joint ablation is required before activation.

halogen_bond_typing.supported_direction: ligand C-X donor to protein acceptor
halogen_bond_typing.ligand_donor_policy: X is neutral Cl, Br, or I with heavy degree one and one single bond to neutral carbon; aromatic and aliphatic carbon are admitted.
ligand_exclusions: halogen bonded to N, O, P, or S
halogen_bond_typing.protein_acceptor_policy: Reuse strict canonical N/O acceptors and their missing-valence axes; add MET SD as the only sulfur acceptor. Plain HIS, CYS SG, unsupported variants, incomplete geometry, cofactors, and ions fail closed.
halogen_bond_typing.radial_policy: Distance is normalized by the Bondi van der Waals-radius sum. No radial Gaussian or element-specific epsilon is used; generic physical LJ owns short-range repulsion.

metal_coordination_typing.supported_scope: Any number of mutually independent active-shell standalone monatomic metal residues. A site receives attraction only when its versioned profile enables attraction and exactly one open coordination slot is resolved from the complete retained receptor/water shell. Other explicitly profiled standalone metals receive bounded all-ligand repulsion and a traced attraction-disabled reason.
metal_coordination_typing.identity_policy: The PDB residue name and element must exactly match a registry key. This admits standalone monatomic ions only. A metal embedded in heme, corrin, chlorophyll, Fe-S clusters, or another cofactor is not reinterpreted as a naked ion.
metal_coordination_typing.attraction_policy: Automatic directional attraction is enabled only for strict Zn(II) tetrahedral and Mg(II) octahedral one-vacancy profiles. Ca, Mn, Fe, Co, Ni, and Cu are registered as repulsion-only because a PDB element record alone does not resolve flexible Ca geometry or transition-metal oxidation/geometry. They remain visible in trace metadata rather than being silently omitted.
metal_coordination_typing.receptor_donor_policy: Static site construction admits close canonical protein O atoms, HIS/HID/HIE ring N atoms, and profile-supported CYS/CYM SG or MET SD atoms. Profile-supported crystallographic water oxygen can complete the Mg shell. Alternate locations, partial occupancy, shared donors, nearby metals, and unsupported close contacts fail closed.
metal_coordination_typing.ligand_donor_policy: Versioned sanitized-graph N/O acceptors and explicit supported S acceptor SMARTS are typed once. A site-specific N/O/S eligibility mask is then applied from the selected metal profile; an ineligible atom is handled by bounded metal non-donor repulsion, never by a hidden zero pair.
unsupported: metal residue and element identity mismatch
attractive profile receptor donor count other than target coordination minus one
site geometry outside the profile RMS tolerance
another metal within the profile cluster cutoff
coordination water under a profile that rejects water
unsupported donor protonation or resonance assignment
metal_coordination_typing.pair_masking: Every admitted metal is absent from generic protein LJ, hydrophobic, hydrogen-bond, and formal-charge masks. Profile-eligible ligand donor pairs at attraction-enabled sites use the directional Morse term. Every other metal-ligand pair receives only the bounded short-range repulsion. Metal Coulomb is inactive.
metal_coordination_typing.activation_policy: metal_coordination is part of the default interaction profile. If a caller constructs a custom profile that removes it while an active-shell metal is admitted, GuidanceEnergy and trace fail with required_interaction_term_inactive.
metal_coordination_typing.coordinate_policy: Site typing and profile selection are static. Metal coordinates, ligand distances, directionality, energy, occupancy, coordination/slot penalties, and non-donor repulsion are evaluated with Torch. No external force-field or docking engine is called.

ZN.distance_provenance: Dokmanic et al. 2008 Table 2; Zn imidazole-N, carboxyl-O/hydroxyl-O collapsed to one O target, and Cys-S structural means.

MG.distance_provenance: Dokmanic et al. 2008 Table 2; Mg carboxyl/hydroxyl/water oxygen structural means.

CA.distance_provenance: Dokmanic et al. 2008 Table 2; attraction disabled because Ca CN6/CN7 geometry is flexible.

MN.distance_provenance: Dokmanic et al. 2008 Table 2; attraction disabled because PDB identity does not determine Mn oxidation state.

FE.distance_provenance: Dokmanic et al. 2008 Table 2; attraction disabled for unresolved Fe oxidation, heme, and Fe-S chemistry.

CO.distance_provenance: Dokmanic et al. 2008 Table 2; attraction disabled for unresolved Co oxidation and corrinoid chemistry.

NI.distance_provenance: Dokmanic et al. 2008 Table 2; attraction disabled because Ni CN4 and CN6 geometry classes are not resolved by element identity.

CU.distance_provenance: Dokmanic et al. 2008 Table 2; attraction disabled because Cu(I)/Cu(II), CN3/CN4, and Jahn-Teller geometry are unresolved.

polar_unsatisfied_proxy_policy.reason: Buried-unsatisfied polarity is a solvation/desolvation statement. The current shell omits complete solvent exposure, water-mediated satisfaction, and not-yet-admitted metal satisfaction, so an energy would create false forces that can expel a ligand from the pocket.
polar_unsatisfied_proxy_policy.eligible_sites: Only already supported ligand N/O donor or acceptor sites are reported.
polar_unsatisfied_proxy_policy.promotion_gate: Requires a separately frozen differentiable burial/solvent contract, water policy, complete satisfying-interaction inventory, numerical admission, and internal held-out ablation.

typing_policy.ligand: Versioned single-atom SMARTS evaluated once with RDKit on the sanitized heavy-atom graph; energy evaluation does not call RDKit.
typing_policy.protein: Versioned canonical standard-amino-acid atom-name tables, expected heavy degree, and canonical heavy-atom bonds; no protein SMARTS or bond-order inference from PDB distance. A degree mismatch, free terminus, chain gap, or missing required neighbor fails closed. Explicit mapped residue variants other than HID/HIE/HIP are excluded from active interaction typing and reported.
typing_policy.hydrophobic_element_policy: Only carbon is an active v1 hydrophobe. S, F, Cl, Br, and I are excluded so weak sulfur and future halogen-bond terms cannot be silently double counted.
typing_policy.hydrophobic_typing_asymmetry: Ligand hydrophobes use a graph SMARTS exclusion around N/O/F, while receptor hydrophobes use a curated canonical residue/atom-name table. This is an intentional representation asymmetry; the two sides share a carbon-only boundary but not one atom-type ontology.
typing_policy.histidine_policy: Explicit HID/HIE/HIP residue names are typed by their declared tautomer/protonation. Plain HIS has ambiguous protonation, so ND1 and NE2 are excluded from v1 hydrogen-bond candidates and counted in trace metadata.
typing_policy.missing_direction_policy: A donor or acceptor without a non-degenerate canonical heavy-neighbor direction or a declared linear/trigonal/tetrahedral geometry is excluded from hydrogen-bond pairs.
typing_policy.direction_geometry_policy: RDKit hybridization and heavy degree define ligand cone targets. Protein N/O cone targets use canonical atom-name geometry: Lys NZ and Ser/Thr hydroxyl O are tetrahedral; other admitted N/O sites are trigonal. These are idealized heavy-atom cones, not reconstructed hydrogen or lone-pair coordinates.
typing_policy.ligand_formal_charge_policy: The sanitized input molecule supplies integer formal charges and the complete protonation/tautomer boundary. Versioned carboxylate, guanidinium, and amidinium SMARTS collapse recognized resonance-equivalent atoms into one equally weighted group site; remaining nonzero formal charges are explicit atom-centered sites. Group membership cannot overlap and the site-charge sum must equal the input molecular formal charge.
typing_policy.protein_formal_charge_policy: Canonical complete side-chain groups only: ARG +1, LYS +1, ASP -1, GLU -1, and explicitly named HIP +1. HID/HIE are neutral; plain HIS, termini, mapped variants/PTMs, incomplete groups, cofactors, metals, and counterions receive no inferred charge and are reported or rejected by the receptor boundary.
typing_policy.formal_charge_site_coordinate: Each group coordinate is the equally weighted centroid of its declared member atoms. This avoids multiplying one residue charge across resonance-equivalent atoms and distributes the Torch gradient back to members by the same weights.
typing_policy.aromatic_policy: Aromatic rings and fused-system membership are deterministic static topology from the sanitized ligand graph or canonical PHE/TYR/TRP and neutral HIS/HID/HIE atom-name tables; HIP is excluded. Ring center, normal, face offset, collapse quality, and every energy value are Torch-coordinate computations.
typing_policy.cation_pi_charge_policy: Only existing complete formal-charge sites with charge exactly +1 e are cations. No partial charge, protonation, or quadrupole is inferred. Ring acceptors are neutral carbocyclic aromatic systems only.
typing_policy.halogen_bond_policy: Only ligand neutral carbon-bound Cl/Br/I donors and strict protein N/O or MET SD acceptors are supported. MET SD uses tetrahedral valence capacity four, expected heavy degree two, and the same missing-valence cone quality machinery.
typing_policy.metal_coordination_policy: The versioned profile registry automatically dispatches standalone monatomic ZN, MG, CA, MN, FE, CO, NI, and CU sites. Strict one-vacancy attraction is enabled only for admitted ZN and complete-shell MG sites. CA and unresolved transition-metal identities are repulsion-only with an explicit trace reason. Cofactors, clusters, identity mismatches, and unregistered active-shell metals fail closed. Site detection is static; coordinate-dependent energy and gradients are Torch-only.
typing_policy.polar_unsatisfied_policy: polar_unsatisfied_proxy is dimensionless trace metadata only. Missing solvent, water, metal, or direction typing never becomes a hidden zero-energy satisfaction assumption.

provenance.hydrophobic_distance_basis: PLIP reports hydrophobic contacts using a 4.0 angstrom heavy-atom criterion; v1 uses a smooth 3.5-to-4.5 angstrom transition around that criterion.
provenance.hydrogen_bond_distance_basis: PLIP reports hydrogen bonds up to 4.1 angstrom with a donor-angle criterion; v1 uses a smooth radial cutoff. Because hydrogens are absent, directionality uses broad idealized missing-valence cones rather than treating the opposite heavy-neighbor axis as a hydrogen coordinate.
provenance.screened_formal_charge_basis: Lee, Fitch, and Garcia-Moreno, Protein Science 11 (2002), DOI 10.1110/ps.4700102, motivates a Debye-Huckel-screened pairwise Coulomb diagnostic and the 25 C water dielectric. kappa=0.127 per angstrom is the rounded value for 0.15 M monovalent ionic strength, 298.15 K, and epsilon_r=78.5. The unit-converted Coulomb prefactor is derived from NIST 2022 CODATA constants.
provenance.formal_charge_limitations: This is an input-state formal-charge-group proxy. It omits partial charges, pKa inference, dielectric heterogeneity, desolvation, polarization, receptor relaxation, cofactors, metals, counterions, and ionic-strength variation.
provenance.pi_geometry_basis: PLIP, DOI 10.1093/nar/gkv315, supplies the 5.5 angstrom, 30 degree, and 2 angstrom aromatic-contact precedent. McGaughey et al., DOI 10.1074/jbc.273.25.15458, motivates separation of parallel and edge-to-face protein aromatic geometry.
provenance.cation_pi_basis: PLIP supplies the 6 angstrom distance precedent. Gallivan and Dougherty, DOI 10.1073/pnas.96.17.9459, supplies the protein cation-pi structural precedent.
provenance.halogen_bond_basis: The IUPAC definition is DOI 10.1351/PAC-REC-12-05-10. Biomolecular Cl/Br/I distance and angle scope follows Auffinger et al., DOI 10.1073/pnas.0407607101. Bondi radii follow DOI 10.1021/j100785a001. Protein carbonyl directionality is informed by Wilcken et al., DOI 10.1007/s10822-012-9592-8.
provenance.metal_coordination_basis: MetalPDB 2024, DOI 10.1107/S2059798324003152, supplies coordination-number, geometry, nuclearity, and site-provenance boundaries. Dokmanic et al. 2008, DOI 10.1107/S090744490706595X, supplies high-resolution PDB structural metal-donor distance targets. Zheng et al. 2008, DOI 10.1016/j.jinorgbio.2008.05.006, motivates fail-closed identity, oxidation, and geometry handling. AutoDock4Zn, DOI 10.1021/ci500209e, remains historical precedent for a zinc-specific directional docking term. EFF-Dock's directional Morse depth/width, occupancy, penalties, and bounded repulsion are diagnostic priors and are not copied docking scores or affinity parameters.
provenance.polar_unsatisfied_limitations: The trace-only proxy is not a solvation, SASA, desolvation, or free-energy model and is forbidden from contributing energy or force.
provenance.coefficient_status: Hydrophobic, hydrogen-bond, charge, pi, cation-pi, halogen, and metal epsilon/width/penalty values not explicitly identified as published geometry are preregistered EFF-Dock diagnostic guidance priors. Structural metal r0 values are not bond free-energy equilibria. No coefficient was fitted to Astex, PoseBusters, crystal energies, RMSD, affinity, Vina, or AutoDock scores.
provenance.external_engine_policy: No external scoring or force-field engine is used. RDKit is restricted to one-time ligand SMARTS typing; all coordinate-dependent values and gradients are computed in Torch.
